distinguishing_features: Direct transfer of flow management principles to solid-state interphase via reversible vacancy buffer
Localized pressure modulation during thermal cycling to actively push voids back into lattice
Use of compliant under-layer to generate controlled pressure gradient opposing vacancy flux
Reversal of net vacancy flux by external pressure gradient below critical nucleation threshold
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Preventing intermetallic Kirkendall void coalescence at wire bond interfaces during high-temperature operation without relying solely on material diffusion barriers
parsed.viable_reason: The required pressure gradient (1 GPa) to reverse vacancy flux is orders of magnitude higher than the 5–10 MPa achievable via compliant substrates, making the mechanism physically infeasible at stated scale.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The concept of actively reversing vacancy flux via external pressure modulation is not an obvious extension of existing diffusion-control or monitoring-based approaches in prior art.
